scenes.text: In November eighteen thirty three, so many meteors fell that people thought the stars were falling.
It happened on the night of November twelfth to thirteenth, over North America.
Observers estimated tens of thousands of meteors every single hour.
Many people were woken up and believed the world was ending.
It's still remembered as the night the stars fell.
A Yale professor named Denison Olmsted noticed something strange.
All the meteors seemed to shoot out from one spot in the constellation Leo.
That spot is called the radiant, and it's why this shower is called the Leonids.
His work helped turn meteors into a real science.
We now know the Leonids are dust from Comet Tempel-Tuttle, which circles the Sun about every thirty three years.
Earth plows through that dusty trail every November.
The grains hit our air at about seventy one kilometers per second.
Most of them are about the size of a grain of sand.
This year the shower peaks around November seventeenth, with only about ten to fifteen meteors an hour.
Would you stay up all night hoping for another storm?

title: The night the stars 'fell' in 1833 🌠
caption: On Nov 12-13, 1833, the Leonid meteor storm lit up North America with tens of thousands of meteors an hour. This year's Leonids peak around Nov 17. 🌠
